source_text: Si ante peccatum per Deum creatum est unde homines nascerentur, per diabolum autem unde parentes commoverentur; adscribitur sine dubio sanctitas nascentibus, et culpa generantibus
pass_a_gloss: If before sin through God creatum is whence human-beings nascerentur, through diabolum however whence parents commoverentur; adscribitur without dubio holiness nascentibus, and fault generantibus.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: If, before sin, God created that from which human beings would be born, while the devil supplied what would stir their parents, holiness is certainly to be ascribed to those born, and guilt to those who conceive them.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
